topics.title: Music

questions.text: Do you prefer sad or happy music?
questions.answer: It really depends on my mood. When I'm feeling sad or tired, I prefer sad music because it somehow connects with my feelings. But when I'm with friends or at a party, happy music definitely makes everything better.
questions.answerZh: 这真的取决于我的心情。当我感到悲伤或累的时候，我更喜欢悲伤的音乐，因为它以某种方式与我的感受产生共鸣。但当我和朋友在一起或在派对上，快乐的音乐绝对让一切更好。

questions.text: Does happy music make you feel more excited?
questions.answer: Yes, definitely! Happy music instantly boosts my mood and gives me energy. It's like a natural medicine — when I hear an upbeat song, I just feel more positive and ready to take on the world.
questions.answerZh: 是的，当然！快乐音乐瞬间提升我的情绪，给我能量。它就像天然的药物——当我听到一首欢快的歌，我就感觉更积极，准备好面对世界。

questions.answer: I started using social media when I was around 14 or 15, mainly Wechat and QQ. At first, it was mainly for fun and keeping in touch with classmates. Looking back, I probably started a bit too early. These days, there's more awareness about age restrictions.

questions.answer: I don't think I spend too much time on social media, but I could probably cut down a bit. I use it mainly for keeping up with friends and news. Sometimes I catch myself scrolling mindlessly for too long, though. Moderation is key.

questions.text: What's your favourite animal? Why?
questions.answer: My favourite animal is probably dogs. What I like most about dogs is that they’ re very loyal and easy to connect with. They seem to understand human emotions quite well, and being with a dog usually puts me in a better mood.

questions.text: Where do you prefer to keep your pet, indoors or outdoors?
questions.answer: I personally prefer to keep pets indoors. For one thing, it’s easier to take care of them and keep an eye on their health. Also, pets are more like family members nowadays, so I feel they should share the living space with us instead of being left outside.
questions.answerZh: 我个人更倾向于把宠物养在室内。一方面，室内更方便照顾，也更容易关注它们的健康状况。而且现在很多人都把宠物当作家庭成员，我觉得它们更适合和人一起生活，而不是被单独放在外面。

questions.answerZh: 有过，但只是在学校的时候。我上学时短暂加入过篮球队，虽然水平一般，但我很享受那种团队氛围。一起训练、一起比赛的过程，也让我学会了如何和别人配合。

questions.text: Is team sports popular in your culture?
Do you like watching team games? Why?
questions.answer: Yes, I do. I enjoy watching team games because they are more exciting and interactive than individual sports. I like seeing how players cooperate with each other, and the atmosphere of team games usually makes the experience more enjoyable.
questions.answerZh: 是的，我喜欢。我喜欢看团队比赛，因为它们比个人项目更刺激，也更有互动感。我很享受看到球员之间的配合，而且团队比赛的氛围通常会让观赛体验更加愉快。

questions.text: What are the differences between team sports and individual sports?
questions.answer: I think the main difference is teamwork and responsibility. In team sports, players need to cooperate and rely on each other, while in individual sports, athletes depend more on their own abilities. As a result, team sports focus more on communication, whereas individual sports require stronger self-discipline.
questions.answerZh: 我认为主要的区别在于团队合作和责任。在团队运动中，运动员需要彼此配合、互相依赖；而在个人运动中，运动员更多依靠自己的能力。因此，团队运动更强调沟通，而个人运动则更考验自律性。我很享受看到球员之间的配合，而且团队比赛的氛围通常会让观赛体验更加愉快。 Morning time

topics.title: Morning time

questions.text: Do you like getting up early in the morning?
questions.answer: It depends. On weekdays, I don’t really enjoy getting up early because I feel quite tired. But if I don’t have much pressure, I actually like early mornings because they’re quiet and peaceful.
questions.answerZh: 这要分情况。工作日我不太喜欢早起，因为会觉得很累。但如果没什么压力，我其实挺喜欢清晨的，那种安静的感觉很好。

questions.text: What do you usually do in the morning?
questions.answer: In the morning, I usually get ready for the day, have a simple breakfast, and check my phone for messages or news. After that, I head out to work or start my daily tasks.
questions.answerZh: 早上我一般会洗漱、简单吃点早饭，然后看看手机里的消息或新闻。接着就出门上班，或者开始一天的事情。

questions.text: What did you do in the morning when you were little? Why?
questions.answer: When I was little, my mornings were quite simple. I usually got up, had breakfast, and then went to school. Everything was arranged by my parents, so I didn’t have to think too much.
questions.answerZh: 我小时候的早晨其实很简单。一般就是起床、吃早饭，然后去上学。因为都是父母安排好的，所以我不用操太多心。

questions.text: Are there any differences between what you do in the morning now and what you did in the past?
questions.answer: Yes, definitely. Now my mornings are more rushed and stressful, while in the past they were much more relaxed. I also have more responsibilities now, so I need to plan my time better.
questions.answerZh: 有的，而且区别挺明显。现在的早晨更赶、更有压力，而以前要轻松得多。而且现在责任更多了，所以我需要更好地安排时间。

questions.text: Do you spend your mornings doing the same things on both weekends and weekdays? Why?
questions.answer: No, not really. On weekdays, my mornings are quite fixed because of work. On weekends, I prefer to slow down, sleep a bit longer, and do things more casually, since I don’t have a tight schedule.
questions.answerZh: 不会。工作日的早晨比较固定，因为要上班。但周末我更喜欢慢下来，睡久一点，做事也更随意，因为时间不那么紧。 Gifts

questions.text: Have you ever sent handmade gifts to others?

questions.answerZh: 有过，但不算多。我做过一些比较简单的手工礼物，比如卡片或者小手工，一般都是送给关系比较亲近的朋友。我觉得手工礼物更有心意，即使看起来不那么专业。

questions.text: Have you ever received a great gift?
questions.answer: Yes, I have. One of the best gifts I’ve received was something I really needed at the time. It wasn’t very expensive, but it showed that the person understood me well, which made it special.
questions.answerZh: 有的。我收到过的一个很棒的礼物，正好是我当时特别需要的东西。虽然不贵，但能看出来送礼的人很了解我，这一点让它变得很特别。

questions.text: What do you consider when choosing a gift?
questions.answer: When choosing a gift, I mainly think about the person’s interests and needs. I also consider the occasion and my budget. For me, a suitable gift is more important than an expensive one.

questions.text: Do you think you are good at choosing gifts?
questions.answer: I’d say I’m okay at it, but not especially good. I usually spend some time thinking and comparing options, but I still feel a bit unsure sometimes. I guess I’ m getting better with experience.
questions.answerZh: 我觉得自己还可以，但算不上特别擅长。我通常会花点时间思考、对比不同选择，但有时候还是会有点不确定。不过我觉得随着经验增加，自己也在慢慢进步。

questions.text: What gift have you received recently?

part3.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of being a famous child?
part3.answer: In general, being a famous child has both advantages and disadvantages. On the positive side, famous children often have access to better resources, such as professional training and financial support, which can help them develop their skills more quickly. However, there are also clear downsides. They may face heavy pressure from public expectations and lose their privacy at a very young age. This can affect their emotional development and mental health in the long run.
part3.answerZh: 总体来看，成为一名有名的孩子既有优势，也有劣势。积极的一面是，他们通常能获得更好的资源，比如专业训练和经济支持，这有助于他们更快地提升能力。但与此同时，问题也很明显。他们从小就要承受来自公众的巨大期待，而且隐私感较弱，这可能会对他们的情绪发展和心理健康产生长期影响。

part3.text: What can today’s children do to become famous?
part3.answer: Nowadays, children have more ways to become famous than in the past. Many of them use social media platforms to share their talents, such as singing, dancing, or creating videos. In addition, some children gain attention through competitions or talent shows. However, becoming famous often requires not only ability, but also guidance from adults and responsible management, especially at a young age.
part3.answerZh: 如今，孩子成名的途径比过去更多。很多孩子通过社交媒体展示自己的才艺，比如唱歌、跳舞或制作视频。此外，一些孩子也通过比赛或才艺节目获得关注。不过，成名不仅需要能力，还需要成年人的引导和合理管理，尤其是在年纪较小的时候。

part3.text: What can children do with their fame?
part3.answer: If managed properly, children can use their fame in positive ways. For example, they can inspire others by setting a good example or raise awareness about meaningful social issues. At the same time, it is important that their fame does not interfere with their education or normal childhood. Fame should be treated as a tool, not the main goal of their development.
part3.answerZh: 如果管理得当，孩子可以将名气用于积极的方向。比如，他们可以通过树立榜样来激励他人，或者帮助提高人们对一些社会问题的关注。但与此同时，也必须确保名气不会影响他们的教育和正常成长。名气应该是一种工具，而不应该成为孩子成长的核心目标。

part3.text: Do people become famous because of their talent?
part3.answer: Talent is certainly an important factor, but it is not the only reason people become famous. In many cases, timing, opportunity, and media exposure also play a significant role. Some people become famous because they meet public demand at the right moment, even if their talent is not exceptional. Therefore, fame is often the result of a combination of talent and external factors.
part3.answerZh: 天赋确实是人们成名的一个重要因素，但并不是唯一原因。在很多情况下，时机、机会以及媒体曝光同样起着关键作用。有些人之所以成名，是因为他们在合适的时间满足了公众的需求，即使天赋并不突出。因此，名气往往是个人能力与外部因素共同作用的结果。 常做计划的人

part3.text: How do young and old people use mobile phones differently?
part3.answer: Young people tend to use mobile phones mainly for social interaction and entertainment. They frequently use social media apps, messaging platforms, and short videos to stay connected with friends and follow trends. In contrast, older people usually use mobile phones in a more practical way. They focus on basic functions such as making calls, sending messages, or using navigation and payment services. Although this difference exists, the gap is gradually narrowing as more older people become familiar with smartphones.
part3.answerZh: 年轻人使用手机更多是为了社交和娱乐。他们经常使用社交媒体、即时通讯软件和短视频平台，与朋友保持联系并关注潮流。相比之下，年长者使用手机的方式更加实用，主要集中在打电话、发短信以及使用导航或支付功能上。不过，随着智能手机的普及，这种差异正在逐渐缩小。

part3.text: What positive and negative impact do mobile phones have on friendship?
part3.answer: Mobile phones have a positive impact on friendship by making communication more convenient and frequent. Friends can stay in touch easily regardless of distance, which helps maintain relationships over time. However, there are also negative effects. Over-reliance on mobile phones may reduce face-to-face communication, leading to shallow interactions. In some cases, misunderstandings can also arise from messages that lack tone or emotional context.
part3.answerZh: 手机对友谊的积极影响在于，它让沟通变得更加方便和频繁。无论距离多远，朋友都可以轻松保持联系，从而维系长期关系。但与此同时，也存在负面影响。过度依赖手机可能减少面对面的交流，使互动变得表面化。此外，由于文字信息缺乏语气和情感背景，也容易产生误解。

part3.text: Is it a waste of time to take pictures with mobile phones?
part3.answer: I do not think taking pictures with mobile phones is a waste of time in most cases. Photos help people record important moments and preserve memories, which can be meaningful in the long run. However, if people focus too much on taking pictures instead of enjoying the moment itself, it may become unnecessary or even distracting. Therefore, the value depends on how and why people use their phones to take photos.
part3.answerZh: 我认为用手机拍照在大多数情况下并不是浪费时间。照片可以帮助人们记录重要时刻、保存回忆，从长远来看具有一定的意义。不过，如果人们过于关注拍照，而忽视了当下的体验，这种行为就可能变得多余甚至让人分心。因此，是否浪费时间，取决于拍照的方式和目的。

part3.text: Do you think it is necessary to have laws on the use of mobile phones?
part3.answer: Yes, I believe it is necessary to have laws regulating the use of mobile phones in certain situations. For example, using mobile phones while driving can cause serious accidents and should be strictly controlled by law. Additionally, regulations in public places such as schools or hospitals help maintain order and safety. Reasonable laws do not limit freedom but instead protect both individuals and society as a whole.
part3.answerZh: 是的，我认为在某些情况下对手机使用进行法律规范是有必要的。例如，开车时使用手机容易引发严重事故，理应受到严格的法律限制。此外，在学校或医院等公共场所制定相关规定，有助于维护秩序和安全。合理的法律并不是限制个人自由，而是保护个人和整个社会的利益。 自行车/摩托车/汽车旅行

part3.text: Should people prepare before giving advice?
part3.answer: Yes, people should prepare before giving advice, especially in serious matters. Preparation helps ensure that the advice is thoughtful and responsible rather than emotional or impulsive. By understanding the situation clearly and considering possible consequences, advisers can provide more useful and practical suggestions. This also shows respect for the person seeking advice.
part3.answerZh: 是的，在给出建议之前，尤其是在涉及重要问题时，人们应该做好准备。充分的准备可以确保建议更加理性和负责任，而不是情绪化或冲动的反应。通过清楚了解情况并考虑可能产生的后果，建议者才能提供更有价值、更实用的意见，这本身也是对寻求建议者的一种尊重。 鼓励别人做不愿做的事

part3.text: Is it good to ask advice from strangers online?
part3.answer: Asking advice from strangers online can be helpful in certain situations, especially when people need different perspectives. Online platforms allow individuals to receive opinions from people with diverse backgrounds and experiences. However, there are also risks. Strangers may not fully understand the situation, and some advice may be unreliable or even misleading. Therefore, online advice should be treated as a reference rather than a final decision-making guide.
part3.answerZh: 在某些情况下，向网络上的陌生人寻求建议是有帮助的，尤其是当人们需要不同视角的时候。网络平台可以让人们接触到来自不同背景和经历的意见。但同时也存在风险。陌生人往往无法全面了解具体情况，有些建议可能并不可靠，甚至具有误导性。因此，网络上的建议更适合作为参考，而不是最终决策的依据。

part3.text: What are the personalities of people whose job is to give advice to others?
part3.answer: People whose job involves giving advice usually need to be patient and empathetic. They must be able to listen carefully and understand others’ problems without judgment. In addition, they are often calm and responsible, because their advice can have a significant impact on other people ’ s lives. Good communication skills and emotional stability are also important traits for professionals in advisory roles.
part3.answerZh: 从事建议类工作的人员通常需要具备耐心和同理心。他们必须认真倾听他人的问题，并且不带偏见地去理解对方。此外，这类人往往性格冷静、有责任感，因为他们给出的建议可能会对他人的生活产生重要影响。良好的沟通能力和情绪稳定性也是这类职业的重要特质。

part3.text: What are the problems if you ask too many people for advice?
part3.answer: Asking too many people for advice can lead to confusion and hesitation. Different people often give conflicting opinions, which makes it difficult to make a clear decision. Moreover, relying too much on others ’         advice may reduce a person ’ s confidence and independence. Instead of trusting their own judgment, they may constantly seek approval, which can slow down the decision-making process.
part3.answerZh: 向太多人寻求建议，容易导致困惑和犹豫。不同的人往往会给出相互矛盾的意见，使得决策变得更加困难。此外，过度依赖他人的建议，可能会削弱一个人的自信心和独立性。与其相信自己的判断，他们可能不断寻求他人认可，从而拖慢决策过程。

part3.text: Why do most children draw more often than adults do?
part3.answer: One reason is that children have fewer responsibilities and more free time. More importantly, children are less afraid of making mistakes and being judged. part3.answerZh: 移动交通工具确实是空气污染的重要来源之一，尤其是在交通密集的大城市，汽车和公交车的尾气排放对空气质量影响很大。不过，我认为它们并不是唯一的污染源。工业生产、发电厂以及建筑活动同样对空气污染起着重要作用。因此，在控制车辆排放的同时，还需要采取更加全面的措施，才能有效改善空气质量。

part3.text: Do you think people need to change the way of transportation drastically to protect the environment?
part3.answer: I do not think people need to change their transportation habits drastically in a short period of time. Sudden changes may cause inconvenience and even social problems. Small but consistent changes in daily transportation choices can make a significant difference in the long run.
part3.answerZh: 我认为人们没有必要在短时间内彻底改变出行方式。过于突然的改变可能会带来不便，甚至引发社会问题。相比之下，循序渐进的转变更加现实。鼓励公共交通、推广电动车以及完善自行车道建设，都有助于减少对环境的破坏。从长远来看，日常出行方式中的小改变，也能产生显著影响。

part3.text: How are the transportation systems in urban areas and rural areas different?
part3.answer: Transportation systems in urban areas are usually more developed and diverse. Cities often have subways, buses, taxis, and ride-sharing services, which provide residents with multiple travel options. In contrast, rural areas tend to rely more on private vehicles or limited bus services. Due to lower population density, public transportation is less frequent and less convenient. This difference reflects the unequal distribution of resources and infrastructure between urban and rural areas.
part3.answerZh: 城市地区的交通系统通常更加完善且多样化。城市中常见地铁、公交、出租车以及网约车服务，为居民提供了多种出行选择。相比之下，农村地区更多依赖私家车或有限的公交线路。由于人口密度较低，公共交通的班次较少，便利性也相对不足。这种差异反映了城乡在资源和基础设施方面的不平衡。 给他人建议

part3.text: Do you think children are born smart or they learn to become smart?
part3.answer: I think it’s a mix of both. Some kids are naturally quick learners, maybe because of their personality or the way their brains work. But in my opinion, what really makes the biggest difference is how they are trained. If a child gets good guidance, practices regularly, and feels safe to make mistakes, they can become much smarter over time. So talent helps, but effort and environment matter more in the long run.
part3.answerZh: 我觉得两者都有。有些孩子天生学得快，可能和性格或大脑方式有关。但我认为真正决定差距的是后天培养。如果孩子有好的引导、规律练习，并且不怕犯错，他们会越来越聪明。所以天赋有帮助，但长期来看努力和环境更重要。

part3.text: How do children become smart at school?
part3.answer: First, they learn by buildingsolid basics, like reading, math, and problem-solving skills. Second, good teachers help a lot, because they can explain things clearly and correct mistakes early. Also, children become smarter when they ask questions and stay curious, instead of just memorizing answers. Finally, working with classmates can train their communication and teamwork, which is also part of being smart.
part3.answerZh: 首先，孩子会通过打好基础变聪明，比如阅读、数学和解决问题的能力。其次，好老师很关键，因为他们能讲得清楚，也能早点纠正错误。另外，孩子愿意提问、保持好奇心，而不是死记硬背，也会变得更聪明。最后，和同学一起合作也能训练沟通和团队能力，这也是“聪明”的一部分。

part3.text: Why are some people well-rounded and others only good at one thing?
part3.answer: I think it depends on their interests and choices. Some people like exploring different areas, so they build many skills step by step. But others may focus on one thing because they want to be excellent at it, or because they don’t have enough time to try everything. Personality matters too—some people enjoy variety, while others feel more comfortable going deep in one field. Both types can be successful, just in different ways.
part3.answerZh: 我觉得这取决于兴趣和选择。有些人喜欢探索不同领域，所以他们一点点积累了很多能力。但也有人只专注一件事，因为他们想把它做到很强，或者时间不够，没法都尝试。性格也有影响——有人喜欢多样性，有人更喜欢在一个领域深挖。两种人都能成功，只是方式不同。

part3.text: Why does modern society need talents of all kinds?
part3.answer: Because modern society is complex, and one type of skill is never enough. For example, we need engineers to build technology, doctors to protect public health, and teachers to educate the next generation. We also need creative people, like designers and writers, to bring new ideas and improve daily life. When different talents work together, a country or a company can develop faster and solve problems more efficiently.
part3.answerZh: 因为现代社会很复杂，只靠一种能力肯定不够。比如我们需要工程师发展科技，需要医生保障健康，还需要老师培养下一代。我们也需要有创意的人，比如设计师和写作者，带来新想法、改善生活。当不同类型的人才一起合作时，一个国家或公司才能发展更快、解决问题更高效。 外国的短期停留

part3.answer: Today, people generally prefer lively and interactive music events, such as pop concerts, music festivals, or live performances by popular bands. part3.answer: In my country, successful movies are usually ones that combine entertainment with emotional appeal. Action and fantasy films often attract young audiences, while family-oriented or inspirational stories appeal to a wider age group. Success often depends not just on the plot, but also on how the movie resonates with people’s emotions and experiences.

part3.text: What are the factors that make a successful movie?
part3.answer: A successful movie usually requires a good script, skilled actors, and professional production. Special effects, music, and cinematography also play important roles. Moreover, marketing and word-of-mouth can determine whether the movie attracts a large audience. Overall, a balance of story, performance, and promotion is key to success.
part3.answerZh: 一部成功的电影通常需要有好的剧本、出色的演员以及专业的制作。特效、音乐和摄影也非常重要。此外，宣传和口碑决定了电影能否吸引大量观众。总体来说，剧情、表演和宣传的平衡是电影成功的关键。

part3.text: Do Chinese people prefer to watch domestic movies or foreign movies?
part3.answer: It depends on age and personal interests. Many young people enjoy foreign movies, especially Hollywood blockbusters, because of their advanced special effects and international fame. part3.answerZh: 这取决于年龄和个人兴趣。许多年轻人喜欢看外国电影，尤其是好莱坞大片，因为特效先进且知名度高。但是国产电影也很受欢迎，尤其是那些关注中国文化、历史或社会问题的影片。总的来说，这两类电影各有观众群体。

part3.text: Do you think only well-known directors can create the best movies?

part3.text: What kinds of jobs need imagination?
part3.answer: Jobs that involve creativity and problem-solving usually need imagination. part3.text: What subjects are helpful for children's imagination?

part3.text: What games help develop children's imagination?

part3.text: How can leaders encourage their employees?
part3.answer: Leaders can encourage employees by giving clear guidance, setting achievable goals, and recognizing their achievements. Positive feedback and constructive advice help employees feel valued and motivated. Moreover, providing opportunities for professional growth and creating a supportive work environment can increase confidence and encourage them to take on challenges.
part3.answerZh: 领导可以通过提供明确的指导、设定可实现的目标以及认可员工的成绩来鼓励他们。积极的反馈和建设性的建议能让员工感到被重视，从而更有动力。此外，提供职业发展的机会并营造支持性的工作环境，也能增强员工信心，鼓励他们迎接挑战。

part3.text: When should parents encourage their children?
part3.answer: Parents should encourage their children whenever they face difficulties or try something new. Encouragement is especially important when children feel afraid, insecure, or lack confidence. By supporting their children at these moments, parents can help them build resilience and develop a positive attitude toward challenges.
part3.answerZh: 父母应该在孩子遇到困难或尝试新事物时给予鼓励。当孩子感到害怕、不自信或缺乏信心时，鼓励尤其重要。在这些时刻支持孩子，可以帮助他们培养抗压能力，并形成积极应对挑战的态度。

part3.text: What kind of encouragement should parents give?
part3.answer: Parents should give encouragement that is positive, specific, and realistic. Instead of just saying “Good job,” they can praise the child’s effort or improvement, such as “You worked really hard on this, and it shows. ” Encouragement should also focus on progress rather than just the outcome, helping children develop long-term motivation and confidence.
part3.answerZh: 父母的鼓励应该是积极的、具体的并且现实可行的。比如，不只是简单地说“干得好”，而是表扬孩子的努力或进步，例如“你在这件事上很努力，效果也很明显”。鼓励还应关注过程而不仅仅是结果，这样能帮助孩子培养长期的动力和自信心。

part3.text: Do you think some people are better than others at persuading?
part3.answer: Yes, I think some people are naturally better at persuading because of their communication skills, empathy, and confidence. They can express their ideas clearly and understand others’ perspectives, which makes it easier to influence people. However, persuasion is also a skill that can be improved through practice, learning, and observing others.
part3.answerZh: 是的，我认为有些人天生在说服别人方面更擅长，因为他们具有良好的沟通能力、同理心和自信心。他们能清楚表达自己的想法，同时理解别人的观点，这让说服别人更容易。不过，说服力也是一种可以通过练习、学习和观察他人而不断提升的技能。 发挥想象力

topics.answer: I want to talk about a time when I encouraged my younger cousin to join a school debate competition. He was very nervous and didn’t want to participate because he thought he would make mistakes and embarrass himself. I encouraged him by reminding him of his previous achievements in speaking and by practicing with him several times. I also told him that even if he made mistakes, it was a good chance to learn and gain experience. At first, he was still reluctant, but after a few practice sessions, he felt more confident and agreed to take part. I encouraged him because I believed he had the potential to do well, and I wanted him to overcome his fear of public speaking.
topics.answerZh: 我想说的是我曾经鼓励我的表弟参加学校的辩论比赛。他当时非常紧张，不想参加，因为他觉得自己可能会犯错误，让自己出丑。我鼓励他的方法是提醒他以前在演讲方面的成绩，并且和他练习了好几次。我还告诉他，即使出错，也是一个学习和积累经验的好机会。刚开始，他仍然有些抗拒，但经过几次练习，他变得更自信，最后同意参加。我之所以鼓励他，是因为我相信他有潜力做得很好，而且我希望他能克服对公开演讲的恐惧。

part3.answer: People usually feel bored when they have nothing interesting to do or when they're in a repetitive situation. For example, waiting in a long queue, sitting through a boring meeting, or being alone with nothing to do can all trigger boredom. Boredom often comes when our brain is looking for stimulation but can't find any engaging activity. Sometimes even when we have free time, if we can't decide what to do, we end up feeling bored. The key is that boredom is a signal — our mind is telling us we need something more interesting or challenging.
part3.answerZh: 人们通常在没什么有趣的事情可做或处于重复性的情境中时会感到无聊。例如，在长队中等待、参加无聊的会议或独自一人无所事事都可能引发无聊。无聊通常来自我们的大脑在寻找刺激但找不到任何吸引人的活动的时候。有时候即使我们有自由时间，如果我们无法决定做什么，最终也会感到无聊。关键是无聊是一种信号——我们的思维告诉我们需要一些更有趣或更有挑战性的东西。
